value.text:
Fourah Bay College is a public higher-education college in the Mount Aureol neighbourhood of Freetown, Sierra Leone. It is a constituent college of the University of Sierra Leone, rather than an independently represented parent university. Founded on 18 February 1827, it has a long history of providing higher education in West Africa. English is listed as its teaching language.

The institution began as an Anglican missionary school established by the Church Missionary Society with support from Sierra Leone's then governor, Charles MacCarthy. Its early students included Samuel Ajayi Crowther. The college subsequently attracted students from Sierra Leone and other parts of West Africa, particularly for theology and education. Between 1876 and 1967 it was affiliated with Durham University. Its original nineteenth-century building was later used for railway administration and as a magistrate court, and it was designated a national monument in 1955.

The college's listed faculties cover arts, engineering, pure and applied sciences, social sciences, law, and applied accounting. A historical account places enrolment at about 2,000 during the 1998/1999 academic year. An undated infobox reports a larger total of 3,465; these numbers should not be compared as a measured trend without their original reporting dates.
